records.section_heading: Protein expression and genetic structure of the coral Porites lobata in an environmentally extreme Samoan back reef: does host genotype limit phenotypic plasticity?

records.question: Did the study observe genetic differentiation of Symbiodinium (symbionts) between corals from the two study locations?
records.ground_truth_answer: No — genetic differentiation of symbionts in corals from the two study locations was not observed.
ground_truth_chunks: Using the common reef-building coral Porites lobata, we investigated (i) coral holobiont (cnidarian host and Symbiodinium) protein expression, (ii) Symbiodinium genetic identity (referred to herein as symbiont), and (iii) cnidarian host population structure in a reciprocal transplant experiment (RTE) between a thermally extreme back reef on Ofu island and the more stable, neighbouring forereef on Olosega.

Genetic differentiation of symbionts in corals from the two study locations was not observed, thus these results suggest a host genetic influence on response differences between corals from contrasting thermal environments.

records.question: When did the reciprocal transplant experiment begin and conclude?
records.ground_truth_answer: The transplant experiment was initiated on 5 February 2005 (day 0) and concluded on 10 February 2005 (day 5).
ground_truth_chunks: The transplant experiment was initiated on 5 February 2005 (day 0) and concluded on 10 February 2005 (day 5).
After an initial 24-h recovery period (day 1), all samples were destructively sampled for four consecutive days (days 2, 3, 4 and 5) between 13:45 and 14:15.

records.question: What primary antibody dilution was used for hsp70?
ground_truth_chunks: Primary antibody dilutions were 1:10 000 for hsp70, 1:5000 for MnSOD, and 1:2000 for Ubiquitin and 4HNE, secondary antibody dilutions were all 1:10 000.

records.question: Which kit and sequencer were used to cycle-sequence the cleaned mitochondrial PCR products?
records.ground_truth_answer: They were cycle-sequenced using the ABI Prism Big Dye Terminator Reaction Kit (PerkinElmer–Applied Biosystems) and run on an ABI-3100 automated sequencer.
ground_truth_chunks: PCR products were treated with 2 U of exonuclease I and 2 U of shrimp alkaline phosphatase (Exo:SAP) at 37 C for 60 min, followed by inactivation at 80 C for 10 min.

Cleaned mitochondrial PCR products were then cyclesequenced using the ABI Prism Big Dye Terminator Reaction Kit (PerkinElmer–Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA, USA) and run on an ABI-3100 automated sequencer.

records.question: What criterion did the authors use to include unique Symbiodinium ITS2 sequence types in their analysis?
records.ground_truth_answer: Unique sequence types were included only if they were found from multiple (three or more) clone libraries or if they matched previously published sequence types.
ground_truth_chunks: Briefly, unique sequence types were only included in the analysis if they were found from multiple (three or more) clone libraries or if they matched previously published sequence types.
The remaining clone singletons were assumed to be errors or rare intragenomic repeats and the nucleotide at the site of polymorphism was converted to the consensus.

Potential psuedogenes were characterized by significant changes to the secondary structure of the ITS2 RNA molecule that probably disrupt correct folding (Thornhill et al. 2007). These sequences were treated similar to singletons and reverted to the consensus sequence as determined by statistical parsimony.

records.question: Which source colonies exhibited elevated levels of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins?
records.ground_truth_answer: Back reef source colonies exhibited elevated levels of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins.
ground_truth_chunks: The most consistent differences observed were the elevated levels of ubiquitin-conjugated proteins in back reef vs. forereef source colonies.

A significant effect of source colony origin was found for all within-day tests while an effect of transplant destination was only significant for two of the five days tested with an opposing direction of difference on day two than day five (Fig. 4).

records.section_heading: Coral host populations show significant differentiation
records.question: What evidence from the section argues against cryptic species causing the differentiation between forereef and back reef populations of P. lobata?
records.ground_truth_answer: Three points argue against cryptic species: all mtDNA and ITS sequences used in the study were found within the monophyletic Clade I containing other P. lobata samples; P. lutea is genetically distinct and falls in an entirely different clade; and the presence of intermediate and shared genotypes in both mtDNA and ITS markers plus a lack of a discernable pattern in the network constructions.
ground_truth_chunks: Also, each mtDNA and ITS sequence used within this study was compared with a recent, comprehensive molecular phylogeny of Porites (Forsman et al. 2009) and all were found to occur within the monophyletic Clade I, a clade containing all other P. lobata samples used in the phylogeny.

P. lutea, the most closely related species morphologically occurs in the region, is readily distinguishable genetically from P. lobata and found within an entirely different clade from all samples used in this study (Forsman et al. 2009).

Additionally, the presence of intermediate and shared genotypes in both the mtDNA and ITS markers (Figs 6 and 7) as well as a lack of a discernable pattern in the network constructions, argue against cryptic species driving the observed pattern of population differentiation.
